questions.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ of three nails is drawn from a population. The population has nails of two different lengths, $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{10}\,\text{cm},$ distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Calculate the standard error of $\overset{―}{X}.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the nails in the population have lengths $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{10}\,\text{cm},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $4+1=5$ nails only with the following lengths:

$$
5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm}\,10\,\text{cm}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot 5+10) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(20+10) \\  & =\frac{30}{5} \\  & =6\,\text{cm},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot {5}^{2}+{10}^{2})-{6}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(200)-36 \\  & =40-36 \\  & =4\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the sample size $n=3,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}=\frac{4}{3}\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}≈1.15\,\text{cm}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$

$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

Since the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=1$ and the sample size is $n=20,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}] & =\frac{1}{20} \\  & =0.05.\end{aligned}

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{0.05}≈0.22.

questions.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ of $n$ bushes is drawn from a population. The population has bushes of two different heights, $4\,\text{ft}$ and $5\,\text{ft},$ distributed in the ratio $3:2.$ Determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than $0.01\,\text{ft}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the bushes in the population have heights $4\,\text{ft}$ and $5\,\text{ft},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $3:2.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $3+2=5$ bushes only with the following heights:

$$
4\,\text{ft},\,4\,\text{ft},\,4\,\text{ft},\,5\,\text{ft},\,5\,\text{ft}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\cdot 4+2\cdot 5) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(12+10) \\  & =\frac{22}{5} \\  & =4.4\,\text{ft},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\cdot {4}^{2}+2\cdot {5}^{2})-{4.4}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(98)-19.36 \\  & =19.6-19.36 \\  & =0.24\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{0.24},$ and we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{0.24}{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.01\,\text{ft}.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{0.24}{n}} & <0.01 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{\sqrt{0.24}}{0.01} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.24}{{0.01}^{2}}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{2\,400} \\ n & >2\,400.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=2\,401.$

questions.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ of $n$ employees is drawn from a population. The population has employees with two different working hours, $38\,\text{h/week}$ and $40\,\text{h/week},$ distributed in the ratio $3:1.$ Determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than  $0.5\,\text{h/week}.$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the employees in the population have working hours $38\,\text{h/week}$ and $40\,\text{h/week},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $3:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $3+1=4$ employees only with the following working hours:

$$
38\,\text{h/week},\,38\,\text{h/week},\,38\,\text{h/week},\,40\,\text{h/week}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(3\cdot 38+40) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(114+40) \\  & =\frac{154}{4} \\  & =38.5\,\text{h/week},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(3\cdot {38}^{2}+{40}^{2})-{38.5}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(5\,932)-1\,482.25 \\  & =1\,483-1\,482.25 \\  & =0.75\,{(\text{h/week})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{0.75},$ and we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.5\,\text{h/week}.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}} & <0.5 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{\sqrt{0.75}}{0.5} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{{0.5}^{2}}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{0.25}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{3} \\ n & >3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=4.$
